title: Embedding fallback, sharding & VDB architecture review
summary: Initial technical discovery for embeddings pipeline and rerank architecture. Customer is testing hybrid search with a vector DB and wants fallback/throughput strategies across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) options. Key concerns: tail latency, sharding, KV/prefix caching, encryption/KMS, and cost tradeoffs for dimensionality and model variants.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Vector DB fallback and sharding patterns
action_items: Jordan Lee - Share benchmark spreadsheet with throughput assumptions and cost estimates - due 2026-11-06
Priya Desai - Run a short latency microbenchmark with 1k qps profile samples and share traces - due 2026-11-09
Aisha Rahman - Provide current vector DB sharding topology and nightly ingest TPS - due 2026-11-07
next_steps: Redwood to send dedicated vs hosted cost comparison + reference architecture (link to doc)
Schedule a 1-hour POC scoping with infra team for private deployment (VPC peering) next week

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-04 22:00 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Maya, Liam, Aisha, Noah (BrightWave)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account, and I have Priya and Samir with me, our SEs. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good thanks, excited to dig in. We've got a lot on the table — embeddings throughput, rerank, and how fallback would work with our vector DB.
[00:15] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: first, we want to understand your current infra and pain points; second, discuss options across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; third, sketch a fallback and sharding approach for hybrid search.
[00:28] Liam: Quick intro from our side: I'm Liam, PM for search. Our infra lead Aisha will cover ops details. We're currently running a custom vector store in k8s using Milvus, about 200M vectors, 768-dim, real-time ingest ~200 TPS, peak query bursts ~1k qps.
[00:45] Aisha: Yeah and we've seen tail latency spikes during marketing pushes. We're trying to reduce cost without sacrificing relevance. Also security — everything must be within our VPC, SOC2+, SSO via Okta, and we need KMS integration.
[00:58] Priya: Awesome context. A couple quick clarifying q's: when you say 1k qps bursts, what percent are rerank calls vs raw vector search?
[01:06] Noah: Roughly 80% are initial ANN lookups (top 200), then we do a rerank stage for about 20% of queries where high-precision matters. Rerank is model-invocation heavy — usually a 2-3x cost delta depending on prompt length.
[01:20] Samir: That's helpful. So hybrid flow is ANN -> candidate set -> rerank. For fallback, do you want Redwood to host the rerank and fall back to a smaller model, or do you prefer falling back to a cached ranking?
[01:33] Maya: We want to avoid an outage on rerank calls. If Redwood is hosting, can you describe Dedicated failure modes and automated fallback?
[01:41] Jordan: Sure. On Dedicated capacity we offer reserved pools; if pods are saturated we can route to a cheaper compatible variant or to Hosted as a fallback. In Private, you control capacity; Redwood's control plane can still manage routing policies via your VPC peering. Priya, do you want to add kernel/latency stuff?
[01:55] Priya: Yeah — from an inference runtime perspective we optimize KV cache reuse and continuous batching. For rerank, small-batch latencies matter: we try to keep tail latency sub-200ms for small models, but larger re-rankers are 300-600ms. We can suggest a two-tier model: compact embedder or quantized reranker as fallback to keep SLA.
[02:14] Liam: How does embedding dimensionality affect cost and throughput? We currently use 768 dims but are open to lower dims if retrieval quality holds.
[02:22] Priya: Vector size directly affects memory and ANN index footprint and search time. Moving to 384 dims can reduce storage and speed up ANN by ~1.6x in our tests, but recall may drop on edge cases. We typically recommend evaluation against your query set. Also model selection: smaller embedding models are cheaper per-encode; Redwood supports batch encode endpoints and prefix caching for repeated queries.
[02:44] Aisha: On the VPC side, would Redwood's hosted option require egress rules? And for KMS, can we bring our own key?
[02:51] Jordan: Hosted will require network peering and restricted egress; for highly regulated customers we recommend Private (customer-managed). For KMS, yes — Dedicated and Private support BYOK via KMS/HSM. Hosted can use Redwood-managed keys but we can discuss a custom arrangement.
[03:07] Maya: We also saw references to prefix/KV caching in earlier docs but not sure how it interacts with our vector DB. Say a query repeats — would you avoid hitting rerank?
[03:16] Samir: If you enable caching, repeated exact prompts or candidate sets can hit cache and skip rerank. Also we can cache dense vectors for recently encoded texts to avoid re-encoding. There's complexity around invalidation with streaming ingest, so we usually scope TTLs.
[03:30] Liam: About sharding — our Milvus clusters are sharded by customer id and time. How would Redwood's fallback work with that topology?
[03:38] Priya: Two patterns: 1) Query-side fanout where Redwood sends requests to your sharded vdb gateways and aggregates, 2) Index-side replication where we keep a compatible ANN replica in Redwood Dedicated to handle spikes. The second adds storage cost but reduces tail latency because we avoid cross-shard scatter.
[03:56] Aisha: Replicating 200M vectors to Redwood sounds expensive and slow to sync. What's realistic?
[04:03] Jordan: For full replication we typically recommend selective replication (hot shards or top-traffic slices). Another approach is storing embeddings in a compressed/quantized variant for the replica, which reduces size and gives acceptable recall for rerank candidates. We'll include sizing numbers in the follow-up doc.
[04:20] Noah: Curious about routing; can Redwood route by latency objective? e.g., first try local VDB, if that fails >200ms route to Redwood-hosted ANN?
[04:29] Priya: Yes, policy-based routing is supported. You can define fallbacks by latency, error rate, or capacity. We also support progressive rollouts and can circuit-break rerank to a cheaper model during sustained saturation.
[04:41] Maya: On security audits, we'd need audit logs for all token-level calls and encryption in transit at TLS 1.3. Do you provide per-route tracing?
[04:49] Samir: We provide token-level cost breakdowns, request/response traces, and customizable retention. For Private deployments logs can be shipped to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[05:00] Liam: One of our main blockers is cost predictability. Can you share a model for tradeoffs between batch size, latency, and unit cost?
[05:08] Priya: Absolutely — batching improves throughput and lowers per-token cost but increases latency. Our Optimize tool simulates batch sizing for your QPS profile; we'll share a spreadsheet modeling different batch and model combos.
[05:21] Maya: Are there examples of customers who run a hybrid model with local vdb + Redwood rerank?
[05:26] Jordan: Yes — several e-comm and media customers run local ANN for primary retrieval and Redwood for rerank. We can anonymize a reference architecture and share a short case study.
[05:36] Aisha: For POC scoping, what minimum data would you need from us?
[05:40] Priya: Sample 10k queries with candidate sets and labels, schema for your vector metadata, current ingest and query traces, and a small dataset for a cold-start replicate if you want us to test replication.
[05:53] Noah: We'll prepare that. Also one technical thing — our index is HNSW tuned with efSearch high for recall but that hurts tail latency. Can Redwood re-rank fewer candidates if ANN recall is high?
[06:02] Samir: Yes — you can tune candidate K (top K) per query class. For high-recall queries we can lower K or use a two-pass rerank where a faster model filters to a smaller set before a heavy reranker.
[06:16] Liam: What about embedding updates? We have streaming upserts — how do you keep cache coherent?
[06:22] Priya: We rely on TTL and incremental invalidation hooks. If you push streaming upserts, you can send invalidation messages to Redwood's cache API. In Private setups you can operate the invalidation endpoint locally.
[06:34] Jordan: Time check — ~15 minutes left. Any remaining hard blockers?
[06:37] Maya: Pricing for replication and guarantees around tail latency are the two biggest unknowns. Also how hard is VPC peering for our infra team?
[06:45] Jordan: For VPC peering we have a checklist: network ranges, firewall rules, and service-accounts. We provide a runbook; the typical setup time is a few days for engineering teams. We'll include the runbook link in follow-up.
[06:57] Priya: For tail latency we can propose an SLO with multi-tier fallback and show simulated traces from the microbenchmark.
[07:05] Liam: Ok cool. Next steps recap?
[07:09] Jordan: Redwood to send: 1) cost/replication sizing spreadsheet, 2) POC scoping checklist and runbook link, 3) case study and reference architecture. BrightWave to send: 1) query samples and traces, 2) sharding topology and ingest TPS.
[07:25] Maya: Sounds good. Let's set the POC scoping meeting for next Tuesday.
[07:29] Jordan: I'll send a calendar invite and attach the docs. Thanks everyone.
[07:33] End meeting

Notes: There are a few transcription artifacts; product names sometimes transcribed (e.g., "red-word large") and KV cache heard as "K-V cash" in places. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.ai/docs/replication-runbook (runbook placeholder), https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/embedding-sizing-spreadsheet (benchmark placeholder).

Primary concerns: tail latency during marketing bursts, cost predictability for rerank, ability to BYOK KMS for Private deployment, and selective replication of hot shards.
